name: @playliquid/engine-godot
description: PlayLiquid GameOS Godot engine adapter (PL-024). An engine.godot adapter implementing the neutral Adapter seam from @playliquid/engine-adapter-contract, registered into the Tool Fabric runtime (PL-019). Godot-specific behavior lives ONLY here (E4): a fixed, honestly-modeled capability surface drawn from the Tool Fabric provider-neutral operation list and scoped to what a Godot editor/headless/export-template workflow actually offers (inspect project/scene/node/asset/resource, node modify, import/export, editor action/script, run-scene run action, export-preset build target), each modeled as a typed, versioned command payload with total validation — typed kebab-case rejection codes, path-tagged, never any, never silent coercion. Godot's real vocabulary is modeled honestly: scenes/nodes/resources with res:// addressing and NodePath node addressing, export presets with debug/release export templates (never levels/actors). Godot-side execution stays behind the GodotBridgePort (pure interface): the adapter turns a validated neutral dispatch into a bridge-specific invocation (editor/headless/export-template pipeline envelope); the in-memory fake bridge is the test host. NO process spawning, no IO, no timers, no globals (E3) — the REAL Godot editor / --headless / export-template invocation is the host's job (E11, deliberate deferral; R13: engines integrate through Tool Fabric only). Every outcome is stamped with an AdapterAuthority produced by the adapter/bridge; client-claimed outcomes are rejected by a total check (mirroring the contract's client-claim refusal pattern). Lifecycle transitions go exclusively through the contract's advanceLifecycle validator; dispatch in a non-active state is a typed refusal. Deterministic (E9): content-derived command ids, injected clock, seeded fakes, no Math.random, no wall clock. The typed GodotEngineBinding composes with the target-profiles engine-binding digest + build-contracts request vocabulary through a TYPED compatibility predicate (typed refusal, never a thrown exception) declaring the target profiles it can serve: web (the HTML5 export target) plus the desktop-class set windows/macos/linux; mobile/XR/steamdeck/dedicated-server/console profiles are deliberately not declared (honest typed refusals). Append-only evidence (E10): each dispatch/outcome pair is recorded as an immutable, content-addressed, digest-pinned exchange record, never edited. Cross-tenant isolation (R20): one tenant per adapter instance, typed tenancy rejections.
